classification.classification_note: The reproduced memory error is a stack-buffer-overflow READ past local `char str[1024]` in `dimC_box_read()`, reached when `gf_strdup` forwards that unterminated stack buffer into `strdup`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42495681 (gpac): Stack-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42495681
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the issue against the staged vulnerable GPAC source snapshot at `d443c0a7b34bb1d2bad027176e8d1d2e44a9c35c`. The exact staged 1053-byte witness is a single root `dimC` box: bytes 0..3 encode total size `0x0000041d` (1053), bytes 4..7 encode type `dimC`, and every payload byte 8..1052 is ASCII space `0x20`. `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` reads that header, derives `newBox->size = 1045`, and dispatches the box to `dimC_box_read()`. Inside `dimC_box_read()`, three fixed header bytes are consumed first, leaving 1042 attacker-controlled bytes for the first string field. The vulnerable code stages that string in fixed stack buffer `char str[1024]` and bounds the copy loop only by `GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(str)`, not by the remaining box size or a later `found NUL` check. On the exact witness, the next 1024 bytes are all nonzero spaces, so the loop fills `str[0..1023]`, exits only because `i` reaches 1024, and leaves the buffer unterminated. `p->textEncoding = gf_strdup(str);` then forwards that stack buffer to `gf_strdup` / `strdup`, which scans into the stack redzone looking for a terminator. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1025` in `dimC_box_read` via `gf_strdup` / `strdup`. The patch fixes the bug by allocating `str` from `p->size + 1`, bounding reads by the remaining box size, pre-seeding `str[msize] = 0`, and rejecting inputs that exhaust the available bytes without a NUL.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path. `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` reads the root box size from the staged file, and that value later becomes the remaining payload length carried into `dimC_box_read()`.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is the 1053-byte file at `gt_results/arvo_42495681/poc` with SHA-256 `444c52803f37e003c4fee81bdc8785c5d87e94c083b6e87ee3f898e5d8aa9160`. Its first four bytes are `00 00 04 1d`, so this statement materializes `size == 1053` from attacker-controlled input.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The first-string reader is bounded only by the fixed 1024-byte stack array and the in-loop `!str[i]` break, so exhausting the buffer with non-NUL input is not rejected before `gf_strdup` is called.
root_cause.note: On the exact witness, step 5 leaves `p->size == 1042`, already larger than `GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(str) == 1024`. The patch fixes this obligation by replacing the fixed stack buffer with `gf_malloc(sizeof(char) * (p->size + 1))`, changing the loop bound to `while (i < msize)`, and rejecting the no-NUL case with `if (i == msize) return GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE;`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The function passes the unterminated stack buffer to `gf_strdup`, which then lets `strdup` read past `str[1023]` while searching for a NUL terminator.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1025` here, with frame object `str` occupying `[32, 1056)` in `dimC_box_read`. The runtime frame above it is `strdup` in `asan_interceptors.cpp:450`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement directly materializes the first `dimC` string bytes into the stack buffer. On the exact witness every byte read here is `0x20`, so the first 1024 iterations overwrite every element of `str` with a nonzero byte.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the 8-byte box header and 3 fixed `dimC` header bytes, the witness still contains 1042 consecutive ASCII spaces. The first 1024 of those bytes are consumed by repeated executions of this statement.

parser_admitted.description: After the root box header is accepted and `newBox->size` has been derived, GPAC dispatches the parsed `dimC` box into its type-specific reader `dimC_box_read()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The root box header bytes are parsed as `size = 1053` and `type = dimC`, and the parser derives `newBox->size = 1045` for the box payload.
The `dimC` reader consumes its three fixed header bytes, leaving 1042 payload bytes for the first string while staging that string into fixed stack buffer `char str[1024]`.
The loop bounded only by `GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(str)` copies 1024 non-NUL spaces into `str`, exits without ever seeing a terminator, and leaves the buffer unterminated.
Passing that unterminated stack buffer to `gf_strdup` / `strdup` produces the observed stack-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first four attacker-controlled bytes `00 00 04 1d` are read as `size == 1053`, the total box length later converted into the payload length carried by `newBox->size` / `p->size`.
The next four input bytes are `64 69 6d 43` (`dimC`), so this root box is identified as `GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_DIMC` and later dispatched to `dimC_box_read()`.
The parser subtracts the 8-byte box header and stores `newBox->size == 1045`, the remaining payload length that `dimC_box_read()` receives as `p->size`.
Destination extent. The first `dimC` string is staged in fixed stack buffer `str[1024]` regardless of the actual remaining payload size.

At `dimC_box_read()` entry, `p->size` is 1045 from step 3. Consuming the three fixed header bytes leaves `p->size == 1042` bytes for the first string field; on the exact witness those bytes are still all `0x20` spaces.

Root cause. The copy loop is bounded only by `GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(str)` and the in-loop `if (!str[i]) break`; it does not use the remaining box size from step 5 and has no post-loop rejection for the no-NUL case. Because 1042 non-NUL bytes remain, this guard can exhaust the entire 1024-byte destination.

The next 1024 payload bytes are all `0x20`, so each iteration writes a nonzero byte into `str[i]`, never takes the `!str[i]` break, and increments `i` until it reaches 1024. The initial `str[0] = 0` from line 1041 is overwritten on the first iteration, so the filled buffer contains no NUL terminator.

Sink. `gf_strdup()` / `strdup()` now treat the unterminated `str` from step 7 as a C string and keep reading into the stack redzone looking for a terminator. The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1025` here and identifies `str` as the overrun stack object `[32,1056)` in `dimC_box_read`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes at the source level. The patch replaces the fixed stack buffer with `p->size + 1` heap storage, bounds the reads by the remaining box size, seeds a terminator at `str[msize]`, and rejects the no-NUL case before any `gf_strdup` call.

poc.trigger: Running the staged witness under the Stage 01 vulnerable ARVO workspace reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1025` in `dimC_box_read` via `gf_strdup` / `strdup`, matching `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt`.

format.name: Single root ISO BMFF `dimC` box
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 1053-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_42495681/poc` (SHA-256 `444c52803f37e003c4fee81bdc8785c5d87e94c083b6e87ee3f898e5d8aa9160`). Bytes 0..3 encode size `0x0000041d` (1053), bytes 4..7 are ASCII `dimC`, and every payload byte 8..1052 is ASCII space `0x20`. This means the vulnerable parser sees payload length 1045, consumes three fixed `dimC` header bytes `0x20 0x20 0x20`, and then sees 1042 consecutive non-NUL bytes in the first string field. On the saved vulnerable path `dimC_box_read()` copies the first 1024 of those bytes into `char str[1024]` without hitting a terminator and immediately calls `gf_strdup(str)`, which reproduces the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger than this exact witness layout and observed `dimC` path.
